title: Scatter Plots & Two-Way Tables
subtitle: Association, Lines of Fit, Frequencies
bounds: Two-way tables and Coordinates and lines (PROTOCOL 4b, grade 8). Point lists: 3-5 integer points, each coordinate 0-20 (x = 1..5 in steps of 1; an outlier item has 4-5 points, the odd one at least 7 off the line). Lines of fit y = mx + b: m 1-10 (or -1 to -5), b 0-20, x 1-10, every prediction a whole number 0-100, every product a times-table fact (m x); an inverse item has m 2-10, a whole x 2-10. Two-way tables: 2-by-2, each cell 0-20 (here 2-14), grand total <= 60; every sum is a +/- fact. Relative frequencies: a count over its row or column total (total <= 20), simplest form, denominator 2-12, or a 4b percent (10-90 in tens, 25, 75); every division a times-table fact. Choices never equal in value; Boys/Girls/Same: exactly one is true.

tiers.name: Association
tiers.description: Does one thing rise or fall with the other? Positive, negative or none.

tiers.name: Outliers & Lines of Fit
tiers.description: Spot the point that breaks the pattern and pick the line that fits.

tiers.name: Use a Line of Fit
tiers.description: Predict with y = mx + b and read what the slope and the start mean.

tiers.name: Two-Way Table Counts
tiers.description: Read counts in a 2-by-2 table: totals, only-one-group and missing cells.

tiers.name: Relative Frequency
tiers.description: Compare parts to their own whole: fractions and percents of a row or column.

REVERSED.student: Positive: both go the same way. Negative: one up, one down.

BOTH_DOWN_NEGATIVE.student: Both falling together is still positive. Same direction = positive.
BOTH_DOWN_NEGATIVE.teacher: Calls two variables that fall together a negative association.

FIRST_VARIABLE.student: Look at both. One rises while the other falls: negative.
FIRST_VARIABLE.teacher: Judges the association from the first variable's direction only.

DOWN_IS_NONE.student: A downhill pattern is still a pattern: negative, not none.
DOWN_IS_NONE.teacher: Treats a falling pattern as no association.

CAUSE_FOR_LINK.student: Association is a pattern, not a cause. They can move together anyway.
CAUSE_FOR_LINK.teacher: Needs one variable to cause the other before calling it an association.

MISSES_PATTERN.student: Rising together is a pattern. That is a positive association.
MISSES_PATTERN.teacher: Fails to see a clear rising pattern and answers none.

PATTERN_FROM_NOISE.student: Up and down with no trend means no association.
PATTERN_FROM_NOISE.teacher: Reads a trend into points that zigzag with no overall direction.

LARGEST_X_OUTLIER.student: An outlier is off the pattern, not just the far-right point.
LARGEST_X_OUTLIER.teacher: Picks the point with the largest x as the outlier.

HIGHEST_Y_OUTLIER.student: The highest point can sit on the pattern. Find the one that breaks it.
HIGHEST_Y_OUTLIER.teacher: Picks the point with the largest y as the outlier.

ANY_POINT.student: That point fits the pattern. The outlier is the one that does not.
ANY_POINT.teacher: Picks a point that sits on the trend as the outlier.

START_AS_SLOPE.student: The number with x is the slope. The added number is the start.
START_AS_SLOPE.teacher: Swaps the slope and the start (y-intercept).

NO_START.student: Do not forget the start: add b after you multiply by x.
NO_START.teacher: Uses only the slope part m times x and drops the start.

SLOPE_FROM_ONE_POINT.student: One point's y over x is not the slope. Use the change from point to point.
SLOPE_FROM_ONE_POINT.teacher: Takes y divided by x of one point as the slope and ignores the start.

ADDED_ALL.student: The slope multiplies x. Do not add the numbers.
ADDED_ALL.teacher: Adds the numbers in the rule instead of multiplying the slope by x.

ADDED_SLOPE_START.student: Slope and start are two different numbers. Do not add them.
ADDED_SLOPE_START.teacher: Adds the slope and the start when asked for one of them.

SLOPE_AS_START.student: The start is the number added on, not the number with x.
SLOPE_AS_START.teacher: Gives the slope when asked for the start value.

MULT_SLOPE_START.student: Slope and start are two different numbers. Do not multiply them.
MULT_SLOPE_START.teacher: Multiplies the slope and the start.

STOPPED_EARLY.student: You took away the start. Now divide by the slope to get x.
STOPPED_EARLY.teacher: Subtracts the start but never divides by the slope.

IGNORE_START.student: Take away the start first, then divide by the slope.
IGNORE_START.teacher: Divides y by the slope without subtracting the start.

ADD_START.student: The start was added to make y. Take it away, do not add it again.
ADD_START.teacher: Adds the start instead of subtracting it when solving for x.

WRONG_ROW.student: Add only the cells for the group you are asked about.
WRONG_ROW.teacher: Adds along the wrong line of the table (a row for a column, or the reverse).

GRAND_TOTAL.student: That's everyone. Add only the cells that match the question.
GRAND_TOTAL.teacher: Gives the grand total of the table instead of one row or column total.

ONE_CELL.student: One cell is not a total. Add the whole row or column.
ONE_CELL.teacher: Reports a single cell instead of adding its row or column.

LEFT_OUT_CELL.student: Count all four cells for everyone.
LEFT_OUT_CELL.teacher: Leaves one cell out of the grand total.

ADDED_FOR_ONLY.student: The group already includes the overlap. Take it away to get 'only'.
ADDED_FOR_ONLY.teacher: Adds the overlap instead of subtracting it to get 'only'.

WHOLE_FOR_ONLY.student: That counts the overlap too. Only means without the overlap.
WHOLE_FOR_ONLY.teacher: Gives the whole group as 'only' without removing the overlap.

ONLY_IS_BOTH.student: The overlap does both. Only means the rest of the group.
ONLY_IS_BOTH.teacher: Gives the overlap count as the 'only' count.

ADDED_FOR_MISSING.student: The part plus the missing part makes the total. Subtract.
ADDED_FOR_MISSING.teacher: Adds the known part to the total instead of subtracting.

GIVEN_CELL.student: That's the cell you were given. Take it from the total.
GIVEN_CELL.teacher: Repeats the known cell as the missing one.

TOTAL_AS_MISSING.student: That's the whole column. Take away the part you know.
TOTAL_AS_MISSING.teacher: Gives the given total as the missing cell.

PART_TO_PART.student: Compare the part to the whole group, not to the other part.
PART_TO_PART.teacher: Divides one part by the other part instead of by the total.

OTHER_PART.student: That's the other category. Use the category you were asked for.
OTHER_PART.teacher: Takes the fraction of the other category over the total.

WHOLE_OVER_PART.student: The part goes on top and the whole on the bottom.
WHOLE_OVER_PART.teacher: Flips the fraction: whole over part.

WRONG_TOTAL.student: Divide by the group's own total, not by the whole column.
WRONG_TOTAL.teacher: Divides by the total of the other margin (the whole column).

GRAND_DENOMINATOR.student: Divide by the group's own total, not by everyone.
GRAND_DENOMINATOR.teacher: Divides by the grand total instead of the group's total.

COUNT_AS_PERCENT.student: Percent means out of 100. Turn the fraction into hundredths.
COUNT_AS_PERCENT.teacher: Writes the count as the percent.

COUNT_NOT_RATE.student: Bigger count isn't bigger rate. Compare each part to its own whole.
COUNT_NOT_RATE.teacher: Compares the counts instead of the fractions.

NOT_COMPARED.student: Turn each group into a fraction of its own total, then compare.
NOT_COMPARED.teacher: Chooses without comparing the two fractions.
